title: GOP Rep. Cory Mills Loses Florida Primary to Ryan Elijah Amid Ethics Investigations
excerpt: Trump's endorsement was not enough to save the scandal-plagued congressman, who lost his central Florida seat to a former TV news anchor.
body:
• Rep. Cory Mills (R-FL) lost his bid for a third term in Florida's 7th Congressional District to former news anchor Ryan Elijah in Tuesday's GOP primary
  • Mills was under investigation by both the House Ethics Committee and the Department of Justice over allegations of campaign finance violations and sexual misconduct
  • The seat is now a potential pickup opportunity for Democrats in November, with Elijah facing former Navy Captain Bale Dalton

Republican Rep. Cory Mills lost his primary election in Florida's 7th Congressional District on Tuesday, defeated by former Orlando-area news anchor Ryan Elijah despite holding a presidential endorsement from Donald Trump. The result is the latest in a string of House Republican incumbents toppled amid personal scandals, adding to Democratic hopes of flipping seats in the 2026 midterms.

NBC News and the Associated Press projected Elijah as the winner, with the former FOX 35 anchor beating out three other Republican challengers, including Mills.

Ethics Probes Weighed Down the Incumbent

Mills had been under mounting legal and ethical scrutiny for months. The House Ethics Committee launched an investigation in November 2025, looking into whether he violated "various laws, rules, or other standards of conduct." A May 2026 update confirmed the probe was also examining a Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Police Department response to a report that Mills had assaulted a woman he was dating.

https://x.com/ThePatriotOasis/status/2089869187292541326

Separately, FOX News reported that the Department of Justice had opened an active criminal investigation into the congressman, though the specific focus remained unclear. Mills also faced a temporary restraining order obtained by a former girlfriend who accused him of threatening to release sexually explicit material.

Mills denied all allegations and compared his legal troubles to those faced by Trump, framing himself as a target of establishment Republicans. He was not charged with any criminal wrongdoing.

Trump Endorsement Could Not Save Him

Despite earning Trump's endorsement, Mills found that the backing was not sufficient to overcome the weight of the investigations. Notably, the Wall Street Journal reported that when Trump issued a batch of endorsements for Florida primary candidates in the days before the vote, he omitted Mills from the list — a potential signal of wavering support.

"These scandals all have a significant impact on the individual races... a disproportionate impact on Republicans' ability to keep their hold in the House this year."

— Erin Covey, House Editor, Cook Political Report

Several prominent Republicans actively backed Elijah over Mills. Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC) led a failed effort to censure Mills and endorsed Elijah. Florida colleagues Reps. Mike Haridopolos and Anna Paulina Luna also threw their support behind the challenger.

What It Means for November

Elijah, who lives in Seminole County with his wife, will face Democrat Bale Dalton — a former Navy Captain and NASA chief of staff — in the general election. The 7th District, which covers Seminole County and portions of Volusia County, was previously seen as safely Republican, but Mills' scandals had already put it on the Democratic target map.

Democrats had flagged the seat as a potential pickup even before the primary, believing Mills' controversies made him vulnerable. With Elijah as the nominee, Republicans may stabilize the race, but the district's competitive dynamics in a midterm environment favoring Democrats could still make it a battleground.

A Pattern for Republicans

Mills joins a growing list of Republican House members brought down by ethics scandals. Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-NC) ended his re-election bid after a House Ethics Committee report accused him of harassing female staffers. Ohio's Rep. Max Miller also faces an ongoing ethics investigation as he seeks re-election.

With Republicans holding a thin 219-212 House majority and four vacancies, losses in competitive districts like FL-7 could be decisive in determining which party controls the chamber after November. The Florida primary results underscore the real-world cost of misconduct allegations in an already tight political environment.
